summary.intent: Complete Phase 23 (Rust SDK extraction) gap closure, run a security review on the new Rust crates, increase test coverage to address Codecov feedback, and get PR #352 merged by fixing CI failures and resolving all review comments.
summary.outcome: All 8 plans for Phase 23 executed and verified; 163 new Rust unit tests added across 3 crates; multiple CI issues fixed (Windows cargo check, cross-language parity); 28+ PR review threads resolved across 4 rounds; PR #352 pushed with security review report included.

repo: Cargo `[patch.crates-io]` applies workspace-wide regardless of feature activation; vendored `fuser` (Unix FUSE) must be kept as a regular optional dep (not target-gated) or Cargo can't resolve `dep:fuser` references in feature definitions on Windows

Moving optional dependencies to `[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]` breaks feature definitions that reference them via `dep:` syntax — Cargo can't resolve the dep on non-matching targets even when the feature is inactive
Desktop crate's `cipherbox-fuse` dependency needs `default-features = false` to prevent the `fuse` feature from activating through the dep chain during `--workspace --no-default-features` builds

CI `cargo check --workspace --no-default-features --features winfsp` — the `winfsp` feature flows through `cipherbox-desktop` to `cipherbox-fuse/winfsp` correctly, but defaults must be explicitly disabled at the dep declaration level too
The `@cipherbox/core` package must be built before `@cipherbox/crypto` in CI (sequential, not parallel) because crypto's test suite imports from core
pnpm setup action (`pnpm/action-setup@v4`) requires explicit `version:` field — omitting it causes the cross-language parity job to fail
Phase 23 introduced 5 new Rust crates: cipherbox-crypto, cipherbox-core, cipherbox-sdk, cipherbox-fuse, cipherbox-api-client
All `KeyState` and `CipherBoxFS` key fields use `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>`; logout calls `KeyState::clear()` and unmount calls `CipherBoxFS::handle_destroy()` for zeroization
HKDF domain separation used across 5 distinct derivation contexts; API client redacts tokens/keys in Debug impls
Ed25519 keypair generation returned bare `Vec<u8>` for private key — fixed to return `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>`; callers in write_ops were wrapping redundantly with `Zeroizing::new()`

code.finding: generate_ed25519_keypair returned bare Vec<u8> for private key, leaving key material in freed memory; fixed to return Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>
ed25519-dalek missing 'zeroize' feature flag in workspace Cargo.toml — SigningKey doesn't zero on drop without it
Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> doesn't implement TryInto<[u8; 32]> directly — must call .into_inner().try_into() to convert
Copy-paste bug: app_version field was being set to device_info.device_id instead of device_info.app_version (caught by Copilot review)
fetch_and_populate_folder and resolve_file_pointers_blocking were dead code — existed in both macOS/Linux and Windows platform paths but had no external callers
IpnsPublishRequest derived Debug, leaking encrypted IPNS key material; replaced with custom Debug impl that redacts sensitive fields
get_bytes method was dead code (never called) and lacked status code checking; removed entirely
encode_libp2p_public_key used 'as u8' cast on key length, silently truncating if key > 255 bytes; fixed to return Result with length validation
Temp directory cleanup was happening before unmount, meaning the mount point could be removed while still mounted; fixed to cleanup after successful unmount on both Linux and macOS
Vendored fuser build.rs called unimplemented!() on Windows (non-Linux without libfuse feature); fixed with early return on cfg(windows)
Mount path was passed as .to_str().unwrap() to Command::arg — should use &mount_path directly to avoid panics on non-UTF8 paths
? operator on logout propagated transport errors before best-effort cleanup path
cipherbox-fuse dependency lacked default-features = false, causing fuse (Unix-only) feature to activate through dep chain during Windows builds

workflow: GSD executor agents can disconnect mid-execution (API ConnectionRefused); spot-checking git log and file state is the reliable way to determine what was actually completed before resuming
1Password SSH agent signing is flaky — sometimes requires 2-3 retries; if it fails consistently, staged files can be committed manually by the user
Running three parallel subagents for crate-specific test writing (crypto/core/sdk) worked well — each completed independently with no conflicts
CodeRabbit generates many review comments per push; batching all fix implementations before replying/resolving saves significant API calls
Security reviews should be committed to the repo (in .planning/security/) and included in PRs, not treated as ephemeral analysis
When adding 163 tests across 3 crates in parallel agents, verifying with 'cargo test --workspace' after all agents complete catches inter-crate issues

friction: 1Password SSH agent signing failed repeatedly, requiring multiple retries and occasional user intervention to commit

Windows cargo check took 3+ iterations to fix: build.rs early return wasn't enough (Rust source still compiled), then target-gating broke feature dep: references, then default-features=false still insufficient due to workspace feature unification
Moving optional deps to [target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies] broke Cargo feature definitions that use dep: syntax — this is a non-obvious Cargo limitation
Cross-language parity failed twice: first from missing pnpm version in action, then from parallel build order (core must build before crypto)
API ConnectionRefused mid-agent-execution lost all in-flight work, requiring manual spot-checking and resumption
CodeRabbit re-raised the ECIES min-size check 3+ times across multiple review rounds despite 'not applicable' explanations
gh CLI error output required multiple different grep patterns to extract actual compiler errors from CI logs
open_items: AES-CTR mode lacks client-side CID verification — attacker controlling the relay could serve tampered ciphertext with predictable bit-flip impact (HIGH finding from security review, not fixed in this session)
file_ipns_private_key in write_ops.rs generates Ed25519 key directly via ed25519_dalek (not through generate_ed25519_keypair) — does not benefit from the Zeroizing return type fix
Codecov coverage for cipherbox-fuse crate (write_ops, read_ops, dir_ops, operations) was not addressed — these have complex FUSE dependencies making unit testing harder
The vendored fuser build.rs early-return fix is a workaround; the proper solution would be removing the [patch.crates-io] entry entirely on Windows builds
~30 test case suggestions from the security review (attack scenarios, integration tests) were generated but not implemented
